stories.headline: Anthropic embeds engineers at NSA to deploy Mythos AI for offensive cyber operations

key_facts.fact: Anthropic has installed about half a dozen forward-deployed engineers inside the US National Security Agency to guide use of its Mythos AI model for offensive cyber operations, the Financial Times reported June 4, 2026

The deployment comes while Anthropic is suing the Pentagon, which labeled the company a 'supply-chain risk' after Anthropic tried to bar government use of Claude for mass surveillance of American citizens and lethal autonomous drones
Anthropic unveiled Claude Mythos in April 2026 to a narrow set of US-based organizations and this week expanded access to 150 organizations across 15 countries

One person close to the situation said Mythos would be useful for infiltrating the networks of nations such as China or Iran; it isn't clear whether Anthropic's engineers are involved in active operations
The model has triggered concern among governments, financial institutions and IT companies over its ability to detect and exploit software vulnerabilities

stories.headline: Anthropic says Claude now writes 80%+ of its code, urges global pause as AI nears self-improvement

key_facts.fact: Anthropic Institute published a report 'When AI Builds Itself' on June 4, 2026 saying more than 80% of code merged into its codebase in May 2026 was authored by Claude, up from low single digits before Claude Code launched in February 2025
The length of tasks AI models can autonomously complete is now doubling roughly every four months, up from an earlier seven-month doubling trend, according to the company's internal data
In a March 2026 poll of 130 Anthropic researchers, the median respondent estimated they produced about four times as much output with Mythos Preview as they would have without access to any AI models

Anthropic called for a globally coordinated mechanism to slow or temporarily pause frontier AI development; head of policy Jack Clark said some models could be capable of recursive self-improvement within roughly two years

Anthropic argued any meaningful pause would require multiple frontier labs across different countries, particularly the US and China, plus verification mechanisms to confirm rivals had genuinely stopped
Anthropic plans to engage lawmakers about recursive self-improvement in the coming months, head of policy Jack Clark said

stories.headline: University of Cambridge trials world's first vaccine with key component fully designed by AI

key_facts.fact: Researchers at the University of Cambridge announced on June 4-5, 2026 the first human safety trial of a vaccine whose key component was designed entirely by AI; findings were published in the Journal of Infection

The team led by Professor Jonathan Heeney fed genetic codes from a range of surveilled coronaviruses into an AI that designed a 'super-antigen' aimed at training the immune system against entire virus families, including mutated and animal-jumping strains
The first trial involved 39 healthy volunteers and was designed primarily to assess safety; researchers reported no significant safety concerns and immune responses against multiple coronaviruses
A Phase II study with about 200 participants is expected to begin soon to gauge how effectively the vaccine trains the immune system
The Cambridge team is already applying the same technology to develop universal seasonal flu vaccines and an H5N1 bird-flu vaccine; Heeney said the AI's capabilities 'exceeded expectations'

organizations: National Institute for Health and Care Research

stories.headline: Cambridge team passes first human trial of an AI-designed 'super-antigen' vaccine

key_facts.fact: University of Cambridge researchers say this is the first time a vaccine's key component has been entirely designed by AI and trialled in humans.
The candidate, called pEVAC-PS, was tested in 39 healthy volunteers aged 18-50 and showed no significant safety concerns or serious adverse events, with results published in the Journal of Infection.

The AI was fed genetic codes of coronaviruses and designed a 'super-antigen' aimed at protecting against an entire family of viruses, including bat-related coronaviruses that have not yet jumped to humans.
The vaccine was developed by Cambridge's Lab of Viral Zoonotics and spin-out DIOSynVax Ltd, sponsored by University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust with primary funding from Innovate UK.
Researchers are now planning a Phase 2 trial in roughly 200 participants and are developing separate AI-designed candidates for flu and Ebola.
Lead researcher Professor Jonathan Heeney said the work converts vaccine development 'from being reactive to being future-proof.'

organizations: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust

stories.headline: Canada launches $2.3B 'AI for All' strategy targeting 250,000 new jobs by 2031

key_facts.fact: Prime Minister Mark Carney launched Canada's national AI strategy on June 4, pledging more than CA$2.3 billion and targeting an additional CA$200 billion in economic growth.
The strategy aims to create up to 90,000 AI-related jobs for young Canadians and 250,000 more jobs through AI adoption by 2031.
Ottawa will put CA$500 million into a new Canadian Tech Growth Fund that will allow the federal government to take equity stakes in promising Canadian AI firms.
The plan targets raising Canadian business AI adoption from about 12% today to 60% by 2034 based on OECD modelling.
Carney said Canada currently 'ranks near the bottom of countries in AI training, in literacy and trust,' framing the strategy as a 'pro-worker' adoption push.

stories.headline: China tightens oversight of its $3.4T private fund industry to steer money into tech

key_facts.fact: China's securities regulator on June 5 tightened oversight of the country's 23 trillion yuan ($3.40 trillion) private fund industry to reduce financial risks and channel capital into tech innovation.

The China Securities Regulatory Commission said it will raise the bar for private fund registration, crack down on illegal fund activities and encourage long-term 'patient' capital for tech-focused venture capital.

The move comes two weeks after Beijing launched a major crackdown on cross-border investment and tightened capital controls, and is part of a broader campaign to direct resources into the tech sector amid Sino-U.S. rivalry.
Regulators will set up a cross-agency monitoring platform to identify risks and misbehaviours and will step up monitoring of government-backed funds.
The new rules extend a clean-up that began in 2023 and has already deregistered more than 5,000 private fund managers.

stories.headline: Coinbase and Better fund first Fannie Mae-backed mortgage collateralized by bitcoin

key_facts.fact: Coinbase and Better Home & Finance Holding Company funded the first Fannie Mae-backed U.S. mortgage using bitcoin as collateral, with a nationwide rollout planned for summer 2026.

The product pairs a standard 15- or 30-year Fannie Mae conforming mortgage with a separate privately-funded crypto-backed loan that covers the down payment, both at the same interest rate and consolidated into one monthly payment.
Collateralization requires 250% for BTC and 125% for USDC, carries no margin calls, and the pledged crypto is held in Coinbase Prime custody and returned upon full repayment.
Better's waitlist already represents about $250 million in potential loan volume, with more than half of interested borrowers planning to buy within six months.

The regulatory pathway was cleared by a June 2025 Federal Housing Finance Agency directive instructing Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac to recognize digital assets as eligible collateral in the $18.5 trillion mortgage market.

stories.headline: China's Daimon Robotics raises 100M yuan Series A from Inovance and China Telecom for tactile robots

key_facts.fact: Shenzhen-based Daimon Robotics completed a 100-million-yuan Series A round jointly invested by Huichuan (Inovance) Industry Investment and China Telecom.
Daimon claims the No. 1 position globally in 'visual-tactile' sensor shipments.
Funds will be used to build a super-large-scale physical interaction information dataset and accelerate the research and development of a physical world model.

Daimon collaborated with Google DeepMind and other institutions on Daimon-Infinity, described as the world's largest full-modal physical world dataset with touch data including texture, hardness and mechanics, with 10,000 hours open-sourced.

stories.headline: Altman-backed fusion startup Helion raises $465M at $15.5B valuation to build Microsoft power plant

key_facts.fact: Helion, the fusion startup backed by Sam Altman, raised $465 million in a Series G funding round at a $15.5 billion valuation.
The round was led by Thrive Capital with new investors including Alta Park Capital, Anti Fund, BoxGroup, Lux Capital, Peak XV Partners and Bill Ford.
Existing investors participating include Lightspeed Venture Partners, Mithril Capital, Dustin Moskovitz via Good Ventures Foundation, and SoftBank Vision Fund 2.
Helion is racing to complete Orion, its first power plant, with an aggressive timeline to deploy fusion power to the grid as early as 2028 under the terms of its deal with Microsoft.
Helion last raised $425 million in January 2025; total funding to date stands at $1.5 billion.

stories.headline: Illinois Gov. Pritzker pauses data-center tax incentives from July 1 amid grid concerns

key_facts.fact: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker directed the state Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity to pause processing new agreements for data-center tax incentives starting July 1.
Pritzker called on lawmakers, labor groups, utilities, local governments and industry leaders to negotiate a permanent framework during the fall veto session.
Since 2019, Illinois has incentivized data-center development, and at least 27 data centers have received incentives totaling $983 million in estimated lifetime tax breaks and benefits.

Pritzker's proposed framework would ban nondisclosure agreements between data centers and local governments, require regular energy and water use reporting, mandate community benefits agreements and require centers to 'go dark' when the grid is strained.
The pause comes after the Illinois POWER Act, which would have curbed data-center development, was not called to a vote in the spring legislative session.

organizations: Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity

stories.headline: Israel-Lebanon ceasefire announced; oil dips on hopes of broader U.S.-Iran deal

key_facts.fact: The U.S. announced that Israel and Lebanon agreed to implement a ceasefire requiring Hezbollah to withdraw south of the Litani River and the Lebanese Armed Forces to take exclusive control of southern Lebanon.
Brent crude fell about 1.6% to $96.25 a barrel and WTI fell 1.3% to $94.73 on June 4 as the ceasefire revived hopes of a broader U.S.-Iran agreement that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

The Republican-led U.S. House approved a resolution on June 3 to block President Trump from continuing the war against Iran; it would need Senate approval and two-thirds majorities in both chambers to override a likely veto.
Trump said negotiations with Iran could see progress 'over the weekend,' while Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said contacts remain open but talks have made no progress.

Despite the ceasefire announcement, an Israeli drone strike wounded several people on the Zefta-Kfarwa Road in southern Lebanon, and analysts warn Strait of Hormuz shipping may take months to normalize.

stories.headline: Obernolte-Trahan unveil bipartisan AI bill that would preempt state laws for three years

key_facts.fact: Reps. Jay Obernolte (R-Calif.) and Lori Trahan (D-Mass.), with Reps. Erin Houchin (R-Ind.) and Scott Peters (D-Calif.), released a 269-page discussion draft of the 'Great American Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026' on June 4, 2026

The bill would preempt state laws and regulation 'specifically regulating the development' of an AI model for three years; states would keep authority to regulate the use or deployment of AI within their borders

Large frontier developers (those with more than $500 million in gross revenue) would be required to publish public AI frameworks covering catastrophic risk, cybersecurity of model weights, critical incident response, and internal misuse mitigations

Developers would retain an Independent Verification Organization licensed by NIST's CAISI for semi-annual audits; they would have to report safety incidents within 15 days and imminent risks within 24 hours

Critics including Americans for Responsible Innovation and Tech Oversight Project warn the bill replaces a state floor with a federal ceiling, freezing child-safety, civil-rights and consumer-protection laws

stories.headline: Kevin O'Leary agrees to halve 40,000-acre Utah AI data center after Senate president's pushback

key_facts.fact: Kevin O'Leary on Thursday June 4 agreed to cut over 20,000 acres from his proposed 40,000-acre data center project in Box Elder County, Utah.

Utah Senate President J. Stuart Adams had on Monday June 1 demanded a 75% reduction, from 40,000 acres down to approximately 10,000 acres, citing public pushback over water use and environmental impact.
The project area being removed is near the Locomotive Springs Waterfowl Management Area and Interstate 80.
O'Leary had initially called Adams's 75% demand 'outrageous,' likening it to selling someone a house and telling them to live in the upstairs toilet.
O'Leary Digital has not yet broken ground or received permits for the project.

stories.headline: OpenAI says it will comply with Trump's voluntary pre-release AI model review order

key_facts.fact: George Osborne, OpenAI's head of countries, told CNBC at SXSW London on June 5, 2026 that the company will sign up to the voluntary framework in President Trump's June 2 executive order requiring AI companies to allow federal government assessment of their models before release

Osborne said it is 'quite right that democratic governments have a big role to play in how this technology is used and deployed' and that the company proactively suggested ways for governments to track safety and security issues

The order requests up to 30 days of pre-release access to 'covered frontier models' and a classified benchmarking process led by the NSA Director to assess advanced cyber capabilities; it explicitly does not create a mandatory licensing or preclearance regime
OpenAI and Anthropic had previously agreed to share pre-release models with the US AI Safety Institute (CAISI) under the Biden administration in 2024

stories.headline: Shifters raises $10.2M seed led by Ace Capital for autonomous defense ground robot teams

key_facts.fact: Shifters announced $10.2 million in seed funding led by Ace Capital Partners, bringing its total funding to $15 million.
Participating investors include Aurelius Capital Management, Corner Ventures, Arkin Capital, STEP World and Fresh Fund.
Funds will support the company's 'Robots Go First' mission to develop supervised autonomous ground robotic systems for defense, security, and critical infrastructure missions.
Shifters has completed demonstrations of coordinated robotic entry and navigation with defense and security stakeholders, with operations in the U.S., Middle East and Europe.

stories.headline: Supabase raises $500M Series F at $10.5B as agents take over database creation

key_facts.fact: Supabase announced a $500 million Series F at a $10.5 billion post-money valuation on June 4, 2026, led by GIC, with Stripe doubling down on a second investment and Salesforce Ventures joining as a new investor
The round comes seven months after Supabase's Series E and roughly doubles the valuation since October, bringing total capital raised past $1 billion

Database launches on Supabase grew 600% in the past year, more than 60% of new databases are launched by an AI tool, and Anthropic's Claude Code has been the largest contributor since the start of 2026
Supabase now has more than 250,000 customers and nearly 10 million developers building on the platform, with 'Supabase for Platforms' recording 370% customer growth in the past six months
Supabase also released Multigres v0.1 alpha, an open-source 'scalable operating system for Postgres' aimed at providing Vitess-grade horizontal scaling

stories.headline: Data center developer Switch in talks to raise billions at $50B+ valuation, eyes 2027 IPO

key_facts.fact: Switch, founded in 2000 by Rob Roy and based in Las Vegas, is in talks with private equity firms including Brookfield Asset Management and KKR to raise billions of dollars at a valuation of at least $50 billion.
Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan investment bankers are advising Switch on the funding effort.
The fundraising round could lay groundwork for a Switch IPO as early as 2027.
Switch counts Nvidia, Tesla and FedEx among its clients and competes in the hyperscale data center market.
The talks come months after SoftBank M&A discussions with Switch reportedly broke down, per The Information's Anissa Gardizy.

stories.headline: US officials in talks with AI companies about taking government equity stakes, NOTUS reports

key_facts.fact: Senior Trump administration officials have held preliminary discussions with major AI companies about the federal government acquiring equity stakes in their firms, NOTUS reported June 4, 2026, citing three people familiar with the matter

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman first pitched the concept directly to President Trump in early 2025 and has revisited it with senior administration officials in recent weeks as a way to distribute AI's economic benefits to the public
Discussions have centered on firms voluntarily ceding shares (not a purchase), with returns potentially directed to public purposes such as a dividend payment to all American households
Anthropic is not in the discussions with the administration about providing equity stakes, a person familiar with the matter told NOTUS

The talks come as Anthropic confidentially filed for an IPO with the SEC on June 1 at a reported $965 billion valuation, while OpenAI prepares its own filing, last reportedly valued at $852 billion in March 2026
Sen. Bernie Sanders met Altman this week and plans to introduce legislation that would transfer 50% of the equity in top AI companies to a public sovereign wealth fund and tax their stock at 50%

The administration in May acquired roughly $2 billion in equity stakes across nine quantum-computing companies, with IBM receiving about $1 billion; Trump earlier converted CHIPS Act grants into a 9.9% stake in Intel

stories.headline: Westmag emerges from stealth with $11M seed led by a16z to build US drone motors and robot actuators

key_facts.fact: Westmag, short for Western Magnetics Company, emerged from stealth on June 4 with $11 million in seed funding led by Andreessen Horowitz, with participation from Founders Fund, Lux Capital, NFDG and Menlo Ventures.
The company is ramping production at Factory 01, its launch manufacturing facility and headquarters in South San Francisco, to fulfill committed orders for hundreds of thousands of units.
Westmag positions itself as a domestic supplier strengthening U.S. robotics, drone, and physical AI supply chains as Chinese suppliers currently dominate actuator manufacturing.

stories.headline: Zelensky publishes open letter to Putin proposing meeting to end the war

key_facts.fact: On June 4, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky published an open letter to Vladimir Putin proposing that the two leaders meet to agree on an end to the war.
Zelensky urged Putin to set a date and venue and warned against prolonging the war into 2027 or 2028, citing intelligence assessments that Moscow is planning for years of continued hostilities.

Putin, speaking to reporters at the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum, said he did not rule out signing a peace deal with Zelensky if an agreement could be reached and was 'willing to make some compromises.'

Overnight on June 4-5, Russia launched two Kh-59/69 guided missiles and 216 Shahed-type drones at Ukraine; air defenses intercepted 198 UAVs. At least 11 people were killed and 68 injured over the past day.
Zelensky's letter argued that ordinary Russians have grown tired of Ukrainian missile and drone attacks, inflation and fuel shortages and were ready for peace.
